title: NCL Mine Surveyor Mock 15
pattern: 100 MCQs, 100 marks, 90 min, NO negative marking

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'photo scale' for a vertical photo is:
questions.solution: Photo scale 1/s = f / (H - h); for example, if f=152mm and (H-h)=3040m, scale is 1:20,000.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: For a tilt correction on a photograph, the 'axis of tilt' is:
options: The line of greatest slope on the tilted photo
questions.solution: The axis of tilt is the line of greatest slope, passing through the principal point and nadir.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'plumb point' (nadir) on a vertical photograph coincides with the:
questions.solution: For a truly vertical photo, the nadir and principal point coincide.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: To compute the height of an object from a single vertical photo, one needs:
options: The scale of the photograph alone
The length of the shadow of the object alone
The photo, flying height, focal length, and the object's base on the ground
questions.solution: Height h = B × f / p where B is the air base (or ground base for a single photo) and p is parallax.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Approaching a goaf, probing shall be carried out ahead of the working for at least:
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 147: the working is probed ahead for at least 1.5 m beyond the last support before approaching the goaf.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'bridge' in aerial photography refers to:
options: Connecting two adjacent strips of photos by common tie points
A physical bridge on the ground
questions.solution: Bridging links adjacent flight strips via tie points for overall network strength.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'radiation condition' in bundle adjustment requires that:
options: All rays from the camera to ground points pass through the lens centre
Ground points are at the same elevation
questions.solution: The radiation (collinearity) condition ensures each ray passes through the exposure station.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'monoplot' is:
options: A single photo with a DEM draped on it for 3D visualisation
A map with the photographic detail overlaid
questions.solution: Monoplotting drapes a single oblique or vertical photo over a DEM for pseudo-3D visualisation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'principal distance' in photogrammetry is synonymous with:
questions.solution: Principal distance = calibrated focal length = distance from perspective centre to image plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: For drone surveys over mining areas, the recommended side overlap is typically:
questions.solution: Standard side overlap for drone mapping is 20-30%; more may be needed in terrain with steep slopes.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'point cloud classification' in LiDAR processing separates:
options: Ground points from non-ground points (vegetation, buildings)
questions.solution: Classification filters ground returns from vegetation, buildings, and other objects.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: While driving approaching old or waterlogged workings, advance boreholes shall be kept at least ______ ahead of the face.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 163: at least 3 advance boreholes not less than 3 m ahead of the face, with flank holes within 5 m on either side.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'photo coordinate system' origin is at the:
options: The nadir point of the photograph
The rear nodal point of the lens
questions.solution: Photo coordinates (x, y) are measured from the principal point, defined by fiducial marks.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: As per CMR 2017, every plan and section at a mine shall be:
options: Serially numbered and stored flat, with indexed field books kept at the mine
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 68: plans and sections are serially numbered, stored flat, and field books indexed and kept at the mine office.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Lens distortion in a metric camera causes:
options: Systematic displacement of image points from their ideal positions
No effect on the positions of the image points
A change in the colour balance of the image
questions.solution: Radial and tangential lens distortions displace points from their true geometric positions.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'tie point' in aerial triangulation is:
options: A point identified in two or more overlapping photos for connection
A point fixed on the ground by theodolite
questions.solution: Tie points link adjacent photos (and strips) but don't necessarily have known ground coordinates.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'block adjustment' in photogrammetry adjusts:
options: The photos of a single flight line alone
An entire block of photos simultaneously
The exterior orientation of one photo alone
questions.solution: Block adjustment handles all photos in a block together, improving overall accuracy.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'epipolar geometry' constrains corresponding points to lie on:
options: Epipolar lines (lines in each photo corresponding to the same 3D point)
The line joining the two perspective centres
questions.solution: Given two photos, a point in one photo must lie on the corresponding epipolar line in the other.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'fundamental matrix' in photogrammetry encodes:
options: The epipolar geometry between two views
questions.solution: The fundamental matrix F relates corresponding points across two views via x'ᵀFx = 0.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'digital terrain model' (DTM) represents:
options: The bare-earth surface without structures or vegetation
All features above the ground surface
questions.solution: DTM (or DEM) shows the ground surface with vegetation and buildings removed.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'section' in mine surveying shows:
questions.solution: A section is a vertical slice showing the vertical extent of workings along a specified line.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Every mine plan or section under CMR 2017 shall show:
options: The magnetic meridian without any reference line
The true north, or the magnetic meridian with the date of the latter
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 64(1)(b): plans show true north or magnetic meridian and the date of the later.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'progress plan' shows:
options: The final layout of the workings after closure
The final layout of the mine
The development and extraction progress at regular intervals
questions.solution: Progress plans record the state of workings at specific dates, showing advance over time.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'contour plan' shows:
options: Lines of equal elevation of the surface or a seam
Lines of equal depth of the seam
Lines of equal slope of the ground
Lines of equal distance from the pit
questions.solution: Contour plans depict terrain or seam elevation through contour lines.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A ' geological section' shows:
options: Subsurface geological formations along a vertical plane
The plan position of the surface buildings
questions.solution: Geological sections illustrate the vertical succession of strata, faults, and seams.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'seam plan' shows:
options: The extent and configuration of a coal seam at a particular level
questions.solution: Seam plans depict the outline, outcrop, and workings within a particular coal seam.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'subsidence monitoring plan' shows:
options: Points of measured surface deformation due to underground mining
questions.solution: Subsidence monitoring plans show measurement points and contours of surface movement.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'pillar and stall' (board and pillar) method leaves coal pillars to:
questions.solution: Pillars are left to support the overlying strata and prevent roof collapse.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'roof bolt' in underground mining is used to:
options: Support the roof by anchoring weak strata to stronger overlying layers
questions.solution: Roof bolts bind together weak immediate roof layers, creating a competent beam.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Under CMR 2017, survey instruments at a mine shall be:
options: Calibrated once a year by the mine
Checked, maintained and calibrated at regular intervals as specified by the manufacturer
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 67(2): survey instruments are checked, maintained and calibrated at intervals specified by the manufacturer.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In opencast mining, a 'bench' is:
options: A horizontal step or ledge in the pit wall
questions.solution: Benches are horizontal levels stepped into the pit wall for safe working and stability.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'highwall' in opencast mining is:
options: The unexcavated face of exposed overburden and coal at the edge of the pit
questions.solution: The highwall is the exposed vertical face at the working edge of an opencast mine.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'dump' in opencast mining is:
options: An area for stacking overburden and waste material
questions.solution: Dumps (overburden dumps) are designated areas where waste rock is deposited.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'haul road' in a mine is used for:
options: Transport of the overburden by conveyor
Carrying water to the working benches
Transport of ore, waste, and equipment by trucks
questions.solution: Haul roads are engineered routes for heavy mining vehicles.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'gradient' of a haul road should be designed to:
options: Be kept at one per cent for all loads
Be limited to two per cent on curves
Allow safe and efficient vehicle operation (typically 8-12%)
questions.solution: Haul road gradients are typically 8-12% to balance haul efficiency and safety.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'batter' in opencast mining refers to:
options: The slope of the pit wall (bench face angle)
questions.solution: The batter angle is the angle of the bench face from the horizontal.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'overall slope angle' of an opencast pit is:
options: The angle of a single bench face
The angle of the steepest single bench face
The angle from the crest of the top bench to the toe of the bottom bench
The angle of the haul road
questions.solution: Overall slope angle considers all benches and berms from top to bottom of the pit.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'berm' in opencast mining is:
options: A horizontal catchment between benches to trap falling material
questions.solution: Berms are safety benches between main benches to catch falling rocks.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'mine plan' is maintained by the:
questions.solution: The mine surveyor is responsible for preparing and maintaining accurate mine plans.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'safety pillar' is left to protect:
options: Surface structures, roads, or water bodies from subsidence
questions.solution: Safety (barrier) pillars protect surface features and prevent water ingress.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'coal dust' in underground mines is a hazard because it:
options: Can cause explosions when dispersed in air with ignition source
Makes the roof strata more difficult to support
questions.solution: Coal dust mixed with air can cause devastating explosions if ignited.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Stone dust barriers are installed in underground coal mines to:
options: Suppress coal dust explosions by diluting with inert stone dust
questions.solution: Stone dust (limestone) is spread to inertize coal dust and prevent explosion propagation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'shot firer' in mining is responsible for:
options: Loading and firing explosive charges safely
questions.solution: Shot firers are trained and licensed personnel who handle blasting operations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When workings extend to within 60 m of the settled boundary with an adjacent mine, the owner/agent/manager shall:
options: Inform the district magistrate and stop workings
Inform the adjacent mine and give its surveyors reasonable facilities for surveys
Stop all work in the mine
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 65(8): the adjacent mine is informed and its surveyors are given reasonable facilities for required surveys and levellings.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Mines Act 1952' is the primary legislation for:
options: Allotment of coal blocks to private firms
Safety, health, and welfare of workers in mines
questions.solution: The Mines Act 1952 comprehensively covers safety, working hours, health, and welfare provisions.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'mine surveyor' must maintain records of:
options: All survey measurements, plans, and sections as per statutory requirements
questions.solution: Statutory records include survey books, plans, sections, and all measurement data.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'reclamation' of a mined-out area involves:
options: Restoring the land to a usable condition after mining
Leaving the area to revert to natural vegetation
questions.solution: Reclamation includes backfilling, grading, topsoiling, and revegetation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'progressive reclamation' approach means:
options: Reclaiming the whole area only at final closure
Reclaiming areas as they are mined out, concurrently with mining
questions.solution: Progressive reclamation restores land in stages as mining advances.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The water-danger plan maintained under CMR 2017 shows water bodies existing within ______ of the boundary of the mine.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 65(1)(g): a water-danger plan and section show water bodies existing up to 200 m of the mine boundary.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'dip' of a coal seam is the:
options: Angle of maximum slope of the seam from the horizontal
questions.solution: Dip is the angle of steepest descent of the seam plane, measured from horizontal.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'fault' in geological terms is:
options: A fracture in rock along which displacement has occurred
questions.solution: A fault is a fracture along which the rock on one side has moved relative to the other.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'vertical shaft' in mining is used for:
options: Storing the mine supplies near the surface
Haulage of personnel, material, and coal; ventilation; and drainage
questions.solution: Shafts serve multiple purposes: hoisting, ventilation, escape, and drainage.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'gradient' of an underground mine road (haulage road) is typically:
questions.solution: Underground haulage roads typically have gradients of 1:10 to 1:8.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'man-riding system' in underground mines is used for:
options: Carrying the mine air along the intake
Conveying workers underground efficiently and safely
questions.solution: Man-riding systems (personnel conveyors, rail-mounted vehicles) transport workers.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'ventilation circuit' in an underground mine ensures:
options: Fresh air reaches all working faces and return air is properly exhausted
questions.solution: Proper ventilation provides fresh air, dilutes gases, and removes dust and heat.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'ventilation door' (stopping) is used to:
options: Block the passage of light into the mine
Control airflow by directing air along intended paths
questions.solution: Ventilation doors/stoppings control the direction and quantity of airflow.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'inbye' direction in a mine means:
options: Away from the shaft, toward the working face
questions.solution: Inbye = toward the working face; outbye = toward the shaft/surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'check measurement' in mine surveying is used to:
options: Verify the accuracy of the main survey
questions.solution: Check (verification) measurements independently verify results for quality assurance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'traverse survey' in underground mines is preferred because:
options: It can advance through narrow headings and is flexible
It is the most accurate method
questions.solution: Traverse methods are well-suited to the linear, constrained geometry of underground workings.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'setting out' of a pillar involves:
options: Marking the pillar boundaries on the floor for extraction or retention
questions.solution: Setting out defines the pillar dimensions and position on the mine floor.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'height of a seam' is measured by the mine surveyor using:
options: Aerial photographs of the seam outcrop
A tape or staff from floor to roof of the working
questions.solution: Seam height (thickness) is measured directly with a tape or staff.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'roof-to-floor' distance in underground mines should be measured at:
options: Points chosen by the workmen on each shift
Regular intervals as specified in the regulations
questions.solution: Roof-to-floor measurements at specified intervals monitor seam thickness and support adequacy.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'cross-section' of a mine is typically drawn on a:
options: Vertical plane along a specified line
questions.solution: Cross-sections show vertical profiles through the mine along a defined section line.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'mine plan book' is a statutory record that must contain:
options: The production and despatches records alone
All survey data, plans, and sections as prescribed by CMR 2017
The record of accidents and dangerous occurrences alone
The list of survey equipment in use alone
questions.solution: The plan book is a legal document containing survey records, plans, and sections.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'level plan' shows workings at:
questions.solution: A level plan depicts workings at one particular elevation or seam horizon.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'coal pillar' design depends on:
options: Depth of cover, seam thickness, and strength of pillars and overlying strata
questions.solution: Pillar design considers depth, pillar dimensions, material properties, and safety factors.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'barrier pillar' separates:
options: Different panels or sections of the mine for safety isolation
The surface and the underground workings
questions.solution: Barrier pillars isolate panels to prevent fire, flooding, or explosion spread.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'Determination of Pillar Strength' formula by Obert and Duvall involves:
options: Only the roof and floor conditions
Only the depth of the seam
questions.solution: Pillar strength is a function of width-to-height ratio and material properties.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'extraction ratio' is defined as:
options: The width-to-height ratio of the pillars
questions.solution: Extraction ratio can be expressed by area or volume; it indicates what fraction of coal is removed.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'geological map' shows:
options: The distribution of rock types and geological structures at the surface
questions.solution: A geological map shows rock units, faults, folds, and other features mapped at the surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'strike' line on a geological map represents:
options: The line of intersection of a bed with a horizontal plane
questions.solution: Strike lines show where a bed intersects a horizontal plane at a given elevation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'dip' of a formation on a geological map is indicated by:
options: An arrow with a number (dip angle) pointing in the direction of maximum slope
A dashed line marking the direction of strike
A tick mark beside the boundary of the bed
A small cross showing the position of the bed
questions.solution: The dip symbol is an arrow pointing down-dip with the angle of dip annotated.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The joint survey plan showing workings near the common boundary with an adjacent mine shall be signed by:
options: The surveyors and managers of both the mine and the adjacent mine
The surveyor and the owner of the mine only
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 65(1)(e): the joint survey plan is signed by the surveyor and the manager of the mine and of adjoining mines whose workings come within 60 m of the common boundary.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Under the Mines Act 1952, an Inspector may, among other powers:
options: Enter, inspect and examine a mine, and make inquiries on any matter relating to safety
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.22: Inspectors may enter, inspect, examine and inquire into any mine and its records.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When workings approach within 60 m of a water body or waterlogged area, the manager shall:
options: Stop working immediately without any plan
Leave the water body untouched forever
Inform the workmen orally about the danger
Prepare a scheme for protection against inrush and drain the water in a planned manner
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 149 (danger from surface water) & Ch. XI: within 60 m, protective schemes (drainage, barriers) are implemented.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In return airways and old workings, the air shall normally contain oxygen not less than ______ and carbon dioxide not more than ______.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 165: not less than 19% oxygen and not more than 0.5% carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: An 'anticline' on a geological map has:
options: Oldest rocks in the centre, youngest on the limbs
questions.solution: In an anticline, the oldest rocks are in the core and youngest on the limbs.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'plunge' of a fold is the angle that the fold axis makes with:
questions.solution: Plunge is the angle between the fold axis and the horizontal.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the percentage of inflammable gas in the general body of air exceeds ______, persons shall be withdrawn from the working.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 166: persons are withdrawn when the general body of air exceeds 1.25% inflammable gas.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'normal fault' is one in which:
options: The hanging wall has moved up relative to the footwall
The hanging wall has moved down relative to the footwall
questions.solution: Normal fault: hanging wall drops relative to footwall (extensional regime).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: A candidate who gets 30% marks fails by 10 marks. Another candidate who gets 40% marks gets 15 marks more than passing marks. What are the passing marks?
questions.solution: Let total = T. 0.30T + 10 = 0.40T - 15 → 25 = 0.10T → T = 250. Passing = 0.30×250 + 10 = 85. Hmm, that doesn't match... Let me recalculate: 0.30T + 10 = pass marks. 0.40T - 15 = pass marks. So 0.30T + 10 = 0.40T - 15 → 25 = 0.10T → T = 250. Pass = 0.30(250)+10 = 85. Not matching options. This question seems poorly constructed.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: If a person covers 10 km in 2 hours, how far will they cover in 5 hours at the same speed?
questions.solution: Speed = 5 km/h. Distance = 5 × 5 = 25 km

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The average of 5 numbers is 20. If one number is excluded, the average becomes 18. What is the excluded number?
questions.solution: Sum of 5 = 100. Sum of 4 = 72. Excluded = 100 - 72 = 28

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: A car travels 150 km in 3 hours. What is its speed in m/s?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F, G are standing in a line. A is third from left. B is to the right of A. C is immediately to the left of B. D is at the extreme right. E is between A and B. Who is immediately to the right of E?
questions.solution: Arrangement: _,_,A,E,_,B,C with D at right end. B is right of E.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.solution: Kosi river is known as the Sorrow of Bihar due to frequent floods.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The southernmost point of India is located in which state/UT?
questions.solution: Indira Point in Great Nicobar is the southernmost point of India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which pass connects Srinagar with Leh?
questions.solution: Zoji La connects Srinagar with Leh in Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following states?
questions.solution: Tropic of Cancer passes through Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB, Tripura, Mizoram — but not Odisha.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which is the largest saltwater lake in India?
questions.solution: Chilika Lake in Odisha is the largest saltwater lake in India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.solution: Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Jog Falls is formed by which river?
questions.solution: Jog Falls is formed by the Sharavathi River in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which of the following is the highest peak in South India?
questions.solution: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala is the highest peak in South India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which canal connects the Bay of Bengal with the Arabian Sea through India?
questions.solution: Indira Gandhi Canal is the longest canal in India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Sundarbans delta is formed by which rivers?
questions.solution: Sundarbans delta is formed by the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which soil type is most suitable for cotton cultivation in India?
questions.solution: Black (regur) soil is ideal for cotton cultivation.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Palk Strait separates India from which country?
questions.solution: Palk Strait separates India (Tamil Nadu) from Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which pass is known as the 'Gateway to the North-East'?
questions.solution: Siliguri Corridor (Chicken's Neck) connects mainland India to the North-East.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian state receives rainfall from both the Southwest and Northeast monsoons?
questions.solution: Tamil Nadu receives rainfall from both Southwest (partial) and Northeast monsoons.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The maximum area under forest cover in India is in which state?
questions.solution: Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover in India by area.
